message: The aggregate found that NFR-6 is ALREADY VIOLATED by merged code, not merely unimplemented. F-4s session-loss path clears staged annotations, and NFR-6 requires them to survive a full disconnect/reconnect cycle without loss. That makes this spec a fix to shipped behaviour rather than a greenfield addition, and it is the only real engineering content here - FR-23 is wiring an ErrorCard that already has the exact required shape to typed states F-2 deliberately left behind. Worth noting F-4 also shipped a VACUOUS session-loss test that passed against deleted code, so this exact area has already produced one false green in this chain. Any test written for NFR-6 must be shown failing before it is trusted.

Discovery livelocks on a cold adb daemon, reproduced on real hardware (Pixel 8, 38031FDJH00JVF). HostCommandTimeoutMs=3000ms is shorter than adb's measured 3.053s daemon cold start, so each poll kills adb mid-daemon-start and the next poll re-enters the same cold state: 41 consecutive timeouts, zero successes, recovering only when a daemon was started manually from a shell. The ProcessRunner pipe-EOF hazard was the first suspect and is RULED OUT - a minimal JVM repro reached EOF on both pipes in 8ms. Full measurements and a suggested fix in inputs/reproduced-defect-adb-cold-start.md. This is shipped-code behaviour and squarely FR-32 (PollFailed) scope.

Binding decision #2 (FR-33) stated its mechanism wrongly and plan drafters A and B both caught it from the code. onSessionLost (MirrorViewModel.kt:182-185) does NOT reach resumeLive's clear logic - it only sets MirrorSession.Lost and nulls sessionDeviceId, leaving currentFrozenFrame and state.frozen untouched. Clearing lives solely in resumeLive (337-340). So the 'involuntary disconnect must stop reaching resumeLive' half of the decision is ALREADY TRUE and implementing it is a no-op. The actual NFR-6 violation is the UI affordance: MirrorAnnotationStage.kt:292-298 offers Resume Live gated on frozen != null alone, and Reconnect exists nowhere in the codebase, so a disconnected user's only action destroys their annotations. Corrected scope: add Reconnect, gate the Resume Live button while session is Lost, leave the button's own behaviour unchanged (protects F-4's AC-51). Critically, AC-54's red run must drive MirrorIntent.ResumeLive while Lost - a test driving onSessionLost alone passes against unmodified main and would be this chain's SECOND vacuous test. Detail in inputs/CORRECTION-nfr-6-mechanism.md.

The design's err-multi body says 'Rectify remembers it until you quit', and the decompose agent judged it already-true via sessionDeviceId. Verified FALSE: sessionDeviceId is a plain MutableStateFlow with no persistence and THREE paths null it - onSessionLost (MirrorViewModel.kt:184, the exact F-3 scenario), selectPlatform (190) and stopSession (246); data-preference-api holds no device-selection key. So the selection survives until the first session drop, not until quit. Same defect class as the comp-02 auto-start copy that presentation-core-ui/CLAUDE.md records as deliberately not shipped. Recommended: change the copy (option 1); optionally preserve across reconnect (option 2, the id is already carried in MirrorSession.Lost where FR-35's Reconnect reads it). Persisting a preference is NEW SCOPE needing its own FR, not a copy string. Detail in inputs/design-error-states.md CORRECTION 3.

T-8 and T-18 (hardware verification: SC-16 cold-daemon recovery, SC-13 physical unplug/replug, ProcessRunner orphan audit) are BLOCKED - adb devices reports an empty list and the Pixel 8 that all of this spec's measurements were taken against has been unplugged. They will be marked blocked rather than complete, and Stage 5 must record them as an open gap rather than a waiver: a waiver implies an accepted risk, this is work that could not be attempted. The virtual-time suite (T1/T15/T16, fake DeviceCommandExecutor) remains the authority for correctness - hardware runs are sanity checks on top of a proof, by the deliberate design recorded in data-device-api/CLAUDE.md. Reproduction steps are in execution/HARDWARE-BLOCKED.md.

T-4's partial work (left by an agent killed mid-flight on an API limit) had AdbHostSourceImpl.startServer() passing HostCommandTimeoutMs (3000ms) while its own KDoc two lines above said DaemonStartTimeoutMs - i.e. the function whose only purpose is surviving the measured 3.03s cold daemon fork was given the exact budget that cannot survive it. The livelock fix would have shipped containing the livelock. It compiled green; the dead agent's compile-only check passed; the test that catches it had already been WRITTEN by that same agent but never RUN. Found by the finishing agent simply running those tests. Standing lessons recorded in execution/NEAR-MISS-t4-budget.md: a written test is not a run test, an interrupted task is unverified however complete the code looks, and when a comment and the code disagree run the test that distinguishes them rather than trusting either. The prescribed mutation also under-killed (moved only one half of the assertion); the agent flagged it and ran three independent mutations instead of accepting a half-proof.

T-11's pre-fix RED run for T2 cannot be captured: the first T-10/T-12 agent was killed mid-flight by an API session limit and reconnect() was already in the tree when the finishing agent arrived, so the pre-fix state no longer existed, and reconstructing it would have needed git writes into a tree five siblings were writing to. Mutation M8 (routing Reconnect through resumeLive) reproduces the identical failure shape permanently as part of the suite, which is stronger as a regression guard but is NOT the pre-fix run. T-11 must say plainly that the pre-fix red was not captured and why, and must not present M8 as if it were. Detail in execution/GAPS-for-later-waves.md.

AC-28's multi-device card may be unreachable: applyDiscovery(Found) never closes the picker and errorCard() deliberately yields to an open picker, so on first discovery the picker wins and the card never renders. Each half is correct per spec but the composition may mean no code path can display the card. T-14 must resolve this rather than assume it away - either AC-28's card is for the later mid-session case (and T-14 proves it reachable there) or something must close the picker on Found (a behaviour change with blast radius against F-2's confirmed picker ACs). Shipping a card no path can display is the FR-37 decorative-button defect relocated from the action to the surface.
